answer: An agent network can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable bond before voting on jobs or claiming rewards; a public ledger records completed work, and independent audits slash the bond when fraud is proved. A Sybil attacker must immobilize real capital for every persona and risks losing it, so spawning cheap accounts buys no influence. The ledge between reputation and trust is narrow: a bond is no relic or nectar of certainty, and checks must resist collusion.
